title: Progressive learning screened single-atom oxide catalysts for acidic oxygen evolution
summary: A progressive-learning workflow combining density-functional theory and machine learning screened 261 single-atom-doped metal oxides and identified nine candidates with predicted OER overpotential below 0.5 V. The publisher abstract reports experimental evaluation confirming predicted activity and durability for Mn single atoms on RuO₂ under acidic conditions. Candidate-wide values are theoretical predictions; only the specified material’s validation is summarized as experimental.
ai_technology: Progressive learning with DFT-derived adsorption-energy features and machine learning
organization: University of Puerto Rico, Río Piedras; Zhejiang University; Shandong University of Technology; Chung-Ang University

source_review.scope: Primary publisher abstract, first-publication date, and author-affiliation metadata; full article and supporting information not reviewed.

evidence.tested: The abstract reports experimental evaluation confirming predicted activity and durability for MnSA-RuO₂ under acidic conditions. The nine candidates and their <0.5 V overpotentials are theoretical screening outcomes, not nine experimental validations.
evidence.unknown: The abstract does not provide detailed experimental conditions or an independent comparison; those are not inferred.
evidence.ai_role: Progressive learning combined DFT with machine learning, using adsorption-energy predictions as auxiliary features to screen single-atom-doped oxide catalysts.
